findings.topic: Unknown recovery result must preserve the global mutation barrier
findings.initial_problem: A valid QueryOperation miss or refusal cleared Pending despite the unresolved originating mutation. Ordinary and typed mutations could then continue.
findings.verified_fix: MovementClientSession retains AmbiguousOrigin across queries and reconnect. QueryMiss/QueryRejected do not clear Pending. Recovery receipts are checked against the full original request. An uncertain write receipt remains globally blocking. A different bridge requires independent fresh instance proof.

findings.topic: An awaited actor transition must not consume the transition interval
findings.initial_problem: Before/after usability booleans alone could remain true while maintenance changed the confirmed actor identity.
findings.verified_fix: EffectEngine compares previous, before-maintenance and after-maintenance identities. It also checks established/useful state before maintenance, so a new acknowledgement cannot retroactively charge unavailable time.

findings.topic: Repeated uncertain receipts must not accumulate acknowledgements
findings.initial_problem: Accept queued an acknowledgement before handling Uncertain, so repeated resolution could enqueue the same receipt on every tick.
findings.verified_fix: Uncertain is handled before acknowledgement enqueue. Remaining acknowledgements are deduplicated. Uncertain records are not acknowledged as successfully cleaned.

findings.topic: Known fault records must permit proven replacement-bridge recovery
findings.initial_problem: An unconditional fault return prevented a ledger without pending publication from discovering the replacement bridge after restart.
findings.verified_fix: Fresh coherent MovementSnapshot identity removes inaccessible old-bridge records and clears only the fault belonging to that old bridge. Same-instance uncertainty stays suspended; no old originals are written into the new bridge.

findings.attribution: Root review, independently checked in final delta
findings.topic: QueryLease Uncertain is distinct from an outstanding publication
findings.initial_problem: Treating every Uncertain response as a transport Pending handle caused ResolveMovementAsync to reject an already acknowledged QueryLease forever.
findings.verified_fix: Accept retains result.Handle only when it equals game.PendingMovement. A known uncertain lease without an outstanding publication follows the fault/replacement-bridge path.

checked_contracts: UInt64 IDs and Float32 values stay binary; all fifteen nonempty field masks are structurally validated.
Shared command semaphore spans publication, wait and response copy. No generic command1466 fallback exists.
Only an immutable correlated receipt establishes ownership; a later snapshot is not substituted for original values.
Lost acknowledgement recovery never republishes Acquire/Reapply/ReleaseIntent blindly. The original intent remains separate from the query handle.
Pending state and monotonic client operation identity survive GameSession reconnect.
Per-actor leases retain unchanged sibling originals and require fresh current identity/values for reapply; native code remains authoritative for compare-and-write.
ReleaseAccepted is durable intent, not proof of completed restoration. Off-current living actors retain cleanup records; retirement is supplied by the native observer.
Current active lease has inspection priority; older pending records rotate by inspection order within the bounded maintenance loop.
Known Uncertain leases and unknown publications are distinct; both remain unavailable for automatic reuse until their respective proof requirements are met.
Initial definite no-write refusals are retryable and bounded by MaxWait. Movement cleanup is not discarded by the scalar cleanup deadline.
All three rewards use only the typed cohort path for Sora, Roxas and Mickey, with no independent scalar restore fallback.
limitations: This is a source review plus verification of existing isolated test logs, not a live game validation or a complete application build.

The fake host journal does not establish native constructor/destructor coverage, memory lifetime, SEH behavior or actual game-thread serialization; separate native evidence and tests cover those contracts.
No frame-exact useful-duration guarantee is made. Long unobserved intervals and identity transitions deliberately charge zero.
An external writer that writes exactly the same value within the same actor lifetime is indistinguishable by value comparison.
Finite native journal/watch capacity fails closed. A missing acknowledgement, unknown lifetime or old living actor can retain cleanup/group reservations.
A fresh bridge invalidates inaccessible old host records; it does not prove that another still-running game process completed its cleanup.
Unexpected native read/observer exceptions outside the commit may leave no typed acknowledgement. They remain uncertain and blocked; no no-write conclusion is inferred.
Review covers the changed movement paths and their shared integration, not every unrelated pre-existing feature in the repository.
